status: draft; astronomical facts, footage, rights and continuity require independent validation

seasons.arc: Season 1 — The Stolen Map | The crew assembles; discovers the Atlas is being altered.

episodes.title: The Parcel Nobody Ordered
episodes.premise: A courier takes a sealed parcel to pay his debts; a customs seizure reveals a deleted coordinate.
episodes.canon_consequence: Jax, Mira and PIP become fugitives.

episodes.title: The Moon Has a Moon Problem
episodes.premise: A relay outage traps the trio in a depot; an escape requires trading the parcel's empty case.
episodes.canon_consequence: An invisible buyer learns the crew's identities.

episodes.title: A Very Small Invoice
episodes.premise: PIP discovers the parcel is an encoded invoice for a nonexistent port; Mira uses timing discrepancies to open it.
episodes.canon_consequence: A ledger fragment points to Mars.

episodes.title: The Red Planet's Red Tape
episodes.premise: A permit officer sells the same landing slot to rival cargo crews; Jax exploits the double booking.
episodes.canon_consequence: Mira finds the first erased port record.

episodes.title: The Man Who Bought a Mountain
episodes.premise: A mining magnate claims a mountain as collateral; the crew must recover its survey before a sham auction.
episodes.canon_consequence: Financier Voss is implicated.

episodes.title: The Phobos Exception
episodes.premise: A tiny moon's station is exempt from port taxes; a fugitive archivist offers proof in exchange for asylum.
episodes.canon_consequence: Veda joins with a damaged checksum.

episodes.title: The Venus Embarrassment
episodes.premise: A floating resort hosts an official summit; the crew poses as caterers to retrieve an access code.
episodes.canon_consequence: The Directorate issues a secret warrant.

episodes.title: Mercury Retroactive
episodes.premise: A cold-trap vault holds decades of falsified shipping bills; PIP invokes an obsolete contract.
episodes.canon_consequence: Voss offers to buy their silence.

episodes.title: A Slight Delay at Ceres
episodes.premise: A water consortium blocks refueling unless Jax arbitrates a debt dispute.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew learns erased ports lost supplies first.

episodes.title: The Last Honest Smuggler
episodes.premise: A rival trader, Cass, auctions a route to a hidden depot; Mira exposes the fake bidders.
episodes.canon_consequence: Cass becomes a reluctant ally.

episodes.title: The Asteroid That Wasn't There
episodes.premise: A tiny survey target is used as a dead drop; the parcel's data points to a false location in the Atlas.
episodes.canon_consequence: A second fragment reveals deliberate censorship.

episodes.title: A Most Inconvenient Storm
episodes.premise: An approaching atmospheric disturbance forces the crew to reroute a delivery while rivals compete for a docking code.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew rescues a witness who knows the erasure schedule.

episodes.title: The Io Job
episodes.premise: Volcanic activity complicates a retrieval from a fictional surface relay; the crew trades a decoy rather than risk a witness.
episodes.canon_consequence: The witness identifies Auditor Pell.

episodes.title: Europa Confidential
episodes.premise: An ice-survey station is covering up falsified scientific logs; Mira wins the staff's trust by exposing the forgery.
episodes.canon_consequence: Pell offers Veda immunity for the original ledger.

episodes.title: No Such Address
episodes.premise: At a trade hearing, the crew proves one deleted settlement exists but cannot establish the scale.
episodes.canon_consequence: Pell confiscates the copy; Veda secretly retains a verification key.

seasons.arc: Season 2 — The Houses of Saturn | Trade families fight over the outer-system gates; the ledger becomes a weapon.

episodes.title: A Seat at the Table
episodes.premise: Voss invites Jax to a family dinner at a fictional orbital habitat; each guest wants a different fragment.
episodes.canon_consequence: Jax learns Voss is paying for gate monopolies.

episodes.title: The Wedding Contract
episodes.premise: A corporate alliance depends on a wedding and a helium-sealed contract; Cass spots a forged clause.
episodes.canon_consequence: A Titan merchant house defects from Voss.

episodes.title: Snow That Knows Too Much
episodes.premise: Plume samples give Mira a reason to visit a research outpost whose logs contradict the Atlas.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew extracts a timestamp proving the cover-up predates Voss.

episodes.title: The Very Quiet Moon
episodes.premise: A retired clerk refuses to testify until the crew locates her missing pension record.
episodes.canon_consequence: Pell's predecessor is identified.

episodes.title: The Two-Faced Estate
episodes.premise: Two heirs claim the same estate; the crew follows inconsistent maps across its bright and dark hemispheres.
episodes.canon_consequence: A family archive reveals the first gate charter.

episodes.title: The Mimas Clause
episodes.premise: PIP discovers a tiny moon's docking permit includes universal emergency access.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew gains a legal loophole, not a physical superpower.

episodes.title: The Hyperion Hotel
episodes.premise: A rotating moon's fictional hotel keeps losing luggage; a rival hides a key in the baggage mix-up.
episodes.canon_consequence: Cass steals the key while Jax apologizes to the wrong guest.

episodes.title: The Ringside Negotiation
episodes.premise: Voss proposes a truce during a shipping hearing; the crew discovers his concessions are already worthless.
episodes.canon_consequence: The houses begin fighting over the ledger.

episodes.title: The Planet on Its Side
episodes.premise: A seasonal forecasting error threatens a merchant convoy; Mira reveals deliberately mispriced insurance.
episodes.canon_consequence: Voss loses the convoy's protection payments.

episodes.title: Miranda's Missing Floor
episodes.premise: A geological map discrepancy conceals a fictional archive access route.
episodes.canon_consequence: Veda recovers an old authorization signed by the Custodian.

episodes.title: The Oberon Papers
episodes.premise: A court historian offers evidence if the crew retrieves her censored manuscript.
episodes.canon_consequence: The Custodian is shown to be an office, not a single person.

episodes.title: Neptune Has Weather
episodes.premise: A storm forecast exposes a trade-house lie; Jax must save a rival ship to secure its records.
episodes.canon_consequence: The rescued captain becomes an independent witness.

episodes.title: The Backward Moon
episodes.premise: A retrograde orbit becomes a clue that a cargo record was fabricated; Cass exposes the double agent.
episodes.canon_consequence: A navigation syndicate takes Voss's place as the immediate threat.

episodes.title: Pluto's Second Appeal
episodes.premise: A frozen-port council demands recognition; its status dispute hides a plot to erase its voting rights.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew wins legal recognition for one independent port.

episodes.title: The Charon Dividend
episodes.premise: The houses convene at a neutral station; Jax offers the charter as leverage and is betrayed.
episodes.canon_consequence: A deep-space coordinate opens, but Voss seizes the ship's credit line.

seasons.arc: Season 3 — The Wandering Worlds | Mythic travelers and literary visitors expand the setting; the crew discovers rival maps.

episodes.title: The Sage at the Empty Gate
episodes.premise: A wandering sage, Narada-inspired Anant, appears at a remote relay and questions what a map is for.
episodes.canon_consequence: He reveals that missing coordinates once protected refugees.

episodes.title: The Seventh Voyage
episodes.premise: Guest Sindbad recounts an earlier voyage whose landmarks match the fragment; a debt collector interrupts.
episodes.canon_consequence: His old itinerary establishes an independent route.

episodes.title: The Dwarf Planet Embassy
episodes.premise: Two diplomats dispute who may claim a remote fictional colony; PIP forces them to read their own charter.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew earns a passport beyond Directorate space.

episodes.title: The Spinning Fortune
episodes.premise: A merchant sells supposedly fixed land plots on a rapidly rotating body; Mira proves the survey misleading.
episodes.canon_consequence: An escrow account funds the crew's next jump.

episodes.title: A Comet's Credit Rating
episodes.premise: A courier cache is accessible only during a scheduled pass; Cass must choose between the key and saving a rival.
episodes.canon_consequence: The saved rival later testifies to a route diversion.

episodes.title: The Man from Sirius
episodes.premise: Guest Micromegas arrives with measurements no official scale can accommodate; the crew brokers mutual understanding.
episodes.canon_consequence: His independent observations disprove a second official map.

episodes.title: A Star Too Close
episodes.premise: A fictional border office denies entry because its risk model assumes an unverified atmosphere.
episodes.canon_consequence: Mira forces a distinction between evidence and speculation.

episodes.title: The Three-Body Dinner
episodes.premise: Three trading delegations refuse to share a banquet table; the seating plan hides a map cipher.
episodes.canon_consequence: An independent council grants temporary sanctuary.

episodes.title: The Moon Princess's Return
episodes.premise: Guest Kaguya's story of a lost home reframes a refugee's disputed citizenship.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew realizes names, not just coordinates, were deleted.

episodes.title: The Perfect Circle
episodes.premise: A census official keeps rejecting residents whose records form a circular dependency.
episodes.canon_consequence: PIP creates an auditable register and recovers erased names.

episodes.title: An Excess of Sunsets
episodes.premise: A two-star setting turns an ambiguous deadline into a contract dispute; Jax exploits conflicting calendars.
episodes.canon_consequence: A courier guild agrees to share its records.

episodes.title: Seven Rooms, One Key
episodes.premise: Seven stations claim ownership of one missing key; a sequential audit reveals a forged chain of custody.
episodes.canon_consequence: Veda identifies a network of witness keys.

episodes.title: An Expensive Breeze
episodes.premise: A fictional orbital resort markets imagined surface tours; Mira exposes the fraud while tracing a hidden account.
episodes.canon_consequence: The account links Voss to an older faction.

episodes.title: The Garden That Wasn't
episodes.premise: Settlers reject a charter describing uncertain habitability as certainty.
episodes.canon_consequence: Anant helps negotiate a fairer agreement; no life is asserted.

episodes.title: The Other Map
episodes.premise: A rival cartographic society reveals the ledger was once a protection tool.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew chooses to search for the original beneficiaries.

seasons.arc: Season 4 — The Republic of Clocks | Time, records and inheritance become the main conflicts.

episodes.title: The Appointment of a Lifetime
episodes.premise: A clock station sends a corrupted time signal; PIP suspects deliberate desynchronization.
episodes.canon_consequence: A witness key must be checked against a new reference clock.

episodes.title: The Bride Who Missed a Century
episodes.setting: S2 orbit near Sagittarius A* (remote simulation)
episodes.premise: A Kakudmi–Revati-inspired family finds its claim invalid after unequal elapsed time on fictional routes.
episodes.canon_consequence: Mira proves the legal clock was altered; no scripture-science equivalence.

episodes.title: The Ticket for Yesterday
episodes.premise: A ticket agency promises past travel; the crew uncovers a simple timestamp fraud.
episodes.canon_consequence: A vanished employee left an audit trail.

episodes.title: The Twin's Complaint
episodes.premise: Two siblings dispute an inheritance after fictional relativistic trips; the double pulsar frames an independent timing check.
episodes.canon_consequence: Pell's office loses a key legal precedent.

episodes.title: The Time Machine That Isn't
episodes.premise: A Wells-inspired inventor sells a device that predicts auction outcomes rather than travels through time.
episodes.canon_consequence: The prediction engine exposes rigged gate auctions.

episodes.title: The Century Deposit
episodes.premise: An old deposit matures on two incompatible calendars; Veda locates the original term.
episodes.canon_consequence: A compensation fund for erased ports becomes viable.

episodes.title: The Last Minute Union
episodes.premise: A shift change synchronized to a pulsar triggers a labor strike; the crew mediates.
episodes.canon_consequence: Workers disclose hidden maintenance logs.

episodes.title: The Man with Two Birthdays
episodes.premise: A witness has conflicting identity records after clock resets; Cass tests the surviving signatures.
episodes.canon_consequence: The Directorate's clock registry is exposed as editable.

episodes.title: A Matter of Seconds
episodes.premise: A tiny timing discrepancy invalidates a mass land seizure; Jax has to argue the claim before a deadline.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew wins an independent audit.

episodes.title: The Clockmaker's Widow
episodes.premise: An archivist's widow refuses to release her husband's work unless his stolen credit is restored.
episodes.canon_consequence: The authorship trail points to the original Atlas designers.

episodes.title: The Too-Early Funeral
episodes.premise: A political leader's estate is distributed before his death is verified; Veda exposes an insurance scheme.
episodes.canon_consequence: A false casualty record leads to a hidden community.

episodes.title: The Wrong Kind of Old
episodes.premise: A fraudulent auction uses uncertain stellar ages as legal proof of antiquity.
episodes.canon_consequence: Mira distinguishes measurement uncertainty from fraud.

episodes.title: The Thirty-Year Lunch
episodes.premise: An elite dinner uses light-travel delays to hide a negotiation; Jax swaps the communication schedule.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew obtains an authenticated old recording.

episodes.title: The Trial of the Clocks
episodes.premise: The timing evidence is presented to an independent tribunal; Pell offers a secret settlement.
episodes.canon_consequence: Veda rejects the settlement and releases the validation method.

episodes.title: The Year That Never Happened
episodes.premise: A missing calendar interval concealed a mass deletion of legal records.
episodes.canon_consequence: A public verdict forces the crew to confront the Custodian's original motive.

seasons.arc: Season 5 — The War of the Maps | Competing ideologies and institutions attempt to seize the open Atlas.

episodes.title: The Department of Other Departments
episodes.premise: The Directorate creates an oversight office whose only purpose is to approve itself.
episodes.canon_consequence: Jax discovers funding for a parallel navigation network.

episodes.title: The Red Star Committee
episodes.premise: A Bogdanov-inspired cooperative debates access to the ledger; a faction tries to privatize the vote.
episodes.canon_consequence: A worker council retains one independent key.

episodes.title: The City of Perfect Agreement
episodes.premise: A Zamyatin-inspired fictional station bans disagreement; a bureaucrat's error makes unanimity impossible.
episodes.canon_consequence: A dissident supplies evidence of coerced consent.

episodes.title: A War of Small Print
episodes.premise: Two suppliers claim exclusive rights to a fictional star-cluster route; PIP finds identical contracts.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew uncovers an intentional monopoly design.

episodes.title: The Planet of Specialists
episodes.premise: A Wells-inspired society assigns one profession to each resident; a missing specialist stalls an appeal.
episodes.canon_consequence: Mira recruits a systems engineer who challenges the Atlas's structure.

episodes.title: The Court of Unreasonable Sizes
episodes.premise: Micromegas arbitrates an argument between civilizations measuring land differently.
episodes.canon_consequence: The parties agree to a common evidence standard.

episodes.title: The Monkey's Promotion
episodes.premise: A Sun Wukong-inspired guest refuses a ceremonial title that carries no authority; chaos reveals hidden appointments.
episodes.canon_consequence: A patronage network is exposed without mocking the sacred tradition.

episodes.title: The Embassy of Birds
episodes.premise: Delegates undertake a collective search for their absent leader; a false claimant sells access.
episodes.canon_consequence: The delegation creates its own council instead.

episodes.title: A Thousand and One Alibis
episodes.premise: A storyteller delays a wrongful conviction by offering linked testimony every night.
episodes.canon_consequence: Cass finds the witness whose story connects the cases.

episodes.title: The Island of Floating Experts
episodes.premise: A panel offers elaborate solutions to a fictional port crisis while ignoring available evidence.
episodes.canon_consequence: Mira makes the overlooked technician the lead investigator.

episodes.title: The Ministry of Empty Space
episodes.premise: An office taxes regions where it provides no services; PIP submits a bill for the office's own absence.
episodes.canon_consequence: The monopoly loses revenue.

episodes.title: The Price of a Photon
episodes.premise: An energy broker charges for publicly observed stellar light as though he owns it.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew establishes a principle of shared navigation data.

episodes.title: The Unperson Register
episodes.premise: A record purge threatens thousands of fictional travelers; Veda proposes an opt-in restoration.
episodes.canon_consequence: The victims retain control of their private records.

episodes.title: The Vote Before the Vote
episodes.premise: A coalition convenes by relay; the agenda secretly predetermines the outcome.
episodes.canon_consequence: Cass releases proof of manipulated procedure.

episodes.title: A Map for Everyone
episodes.premise: The crew publishes a redacted open Atlas; a malicious faction exploits what remains hidden.
episodes.canon_consequence: A rescue signal identifies the next season's refuge network.

seasons.arc: Season 6 — The Refugee Routes | The cost of openness becomes clear; the crew chooses consent over control.

episodes.title: The Missing Passenger List
episodes.premise: An anonymous manifest hides survivors and criminals alike; Veda establishes consent-based verification.
episodes.canon_consequence: A former Custodian offers help.

episodes.title: The Long Night Ferry
episodes.premise: A distant relay transmits an apparent refugee distress call; Cass discovers an extortion attempt.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew protects a genuine route without exposing it.

episodes.title: The Dark Forest, Politely
episodes.premise: A settlement fears being detected; two captains dispute how to contact it.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew negotiates a voluntary contact protocol.

episodes.title: The Ocean Under Ice
episodes.premise: A hidden shelter faces a resource dispute; a plume-research project supplies logistical context, not proof of life.
episodes.canon_consequence: Veda brokers a safe evacuation agreement.

episodes.title: A Thousand Doors
episodes.premise: Different shelters use incompatible identity systems; PIP builds a privacy-preserving translation method.
episodes.canon_consequence: Refugees can authenticate without publishing coordinates.

episodes.title: The Island That Was a Whale
episodes.premise: A Sindbad-inspired misidentified haven turns out to be an abandoned moving depot.
episodes.canon_consequence: Cass rescues people before salvaging the cargo.

episodes.title: The Guest Who Never Left
episodes.premise: A family hosts a fugitive who is also a witness against their sponsor.
episodes.canon_consequence: Jax chooses the guest over a lucrative contract.

episodes.title: The Invisible City
episodes.premise: An obscured fictional refuge is accused of fraud because outsiders cannot see it optically.
episodes.canon_consequence: Mira demonstrates evidence can depend on wavelength.

episodes.title: The Last Bridge
episodes.premise: Two communities need a shared communications relay but refuse common governance.
episodes.canon_consequence: A temporary mutual-aid agreement becomes a model.

episodes.title: The Great Silence
episodes.premise: A missing response is mistaken for a hostile act; the crew waits for independently verified evidence.
episodes.canon_consequence: A forged message campaign is uncovered.

episodes.title: The Name That Belongs to Me
episodes.premise: A broker trades people's identities as credentials; Veda helps a claimant regain control.
episodes.canon_consequence: Pell secretly supplies an incriminating ledger entry.

episodes.title: The Flood Archive
episodes.premise: A Markandeya-inspired tale of surviving dissolution frames a debate about saving records after disaster.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew preserves testimony, not a monopoly over history.

episodes.title: The Garden of the Exiles
episodes.premise: Refugees disagree about settling an uncharacterized planet; Mira refuses to invent habitability.
episodes.canon_consequence: A safer fictional orbital haven is chosen.

episodes.title: The Custodian's Confession
episodes.premise: The former Custodian admits the first map redactions protected threatened travelers; later officials captured the system.
episodes.canon_consequence: Voss intends to purchase the remaining hidden routes.

episodes.title: The Door We Keep Closed
episodes.premise: The crew defeats a forced-disclosure vote while keeping governance transparent.
episodes.canon_consequence: A distributed consent charter is born; Voss turns to information warfare.

seasons.arc: Season 7 — The Counterfeit Universe | Forged evidence, impersonation and control of narratives test the crew.

episodes.title: The Photograph of Tomorrow
episodes.premise: A sensational image is sold as an immediate view of events; Mira exposes the misuse of light-travel time.
episodes.canon_consequence: A forged Atlas image gains traction anyway.

episodes.title: The Planet That Looked Like Home
episodes.premise: An advertisement promises a second Earth using invented imagery; refugees nearly buy passage.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew establishes an observed/inferred/fiction label system.

episodes.title: The Double of Captain Jax
episodes.premise: An impersonator signs a debt in Jax's name; PIP checks provenance, not appearance.
episodes.canon_consequence: Jax discovers someone is manufacturing witnesses.

episodes.title: The Unreliable Narrator
episodes.premise: A serial storyteller offers contradictory versions of a trade war; Veda compares independent records.
episodes.canon_consequence: The original testimony survives the edits.

episodes.title: The Auction of a Supernova
episodes.premise: A fraudster sells a duplicate historic explosion as live spectacle; Cass reverses the auction.
episodes.canon_consequence: The counterfeiter identifies a propaganda syndicate.

episodes.title: A Telescope with an Agenda
episodes.premise: A survey contractor suppresses inconvenient wavelengths; Mira commissions independent analysis.
episodes.canon_consequence: The coalition adopts cross-source verification.

episodes.title: The Most Famous Nobody
episodes.premise: A manufactured celebrity endorses a false route; the crew tracks the empty corporate record.
episodes.canon_consequence: Voss is tied to the synthetic persona network.

episodes.title: The Echo Chamber
episodes.premise: A light-echo visualization inspires a plot about repeated reports mistaken for independent corroboration.
episodes.canon_consequence: PIP deduplicates evidence and finds its origin.

episodes.title: The Letter from Andromeda
episodes.premise: A purported urgent letter contradicts ordinary light-travel times; a fictional gate route is tested separately.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew exposes a fake emergency while respecting the invented travel rule.

episodes.title: The Hundredth Lie
episodes.premise: Voss offers a public debate built on a false premise; the crew declines the trap and releases primary evidence.
episodes.canon_consequence: Pell openly defects and brings the original archive index.

episodes.title: The Man Who Owned a Constellation
episodes.premise: A promoter sells imaginary ownership of unrelated stars; Jax challenges the contracts.
episodes.canon_consequence: Recovered funds pay for witness protection.

episodes.title: The Archive of Lost Voices
episodes.premise: A disputed testimony is split across many media; Cass retrieves independent copies.
episodes.canon_consequence: The archive demonstrates that the Custodian's charter was rewritten.

episodes.title: The Wrong Galaxy
episodes.premise: A reconstruction is mistaken for a map of a fictional colony; Mira separates simulation from observation.
episodes.canon_consequence: A fabricated route is closed before passengers depart.

episodes.title: The Honest Mistake
episodes.premise: A respected scientist corrects a mistaken identification; Voss weaponizes the correction.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew defends honest uncertainty and finds intentional fraud elsewhere.

episodes.title: The Public Record
episodes.premise: The coalition publishes a verifiable history of the erasures; Voss escapes responsibility by buying debt.
episodes.canon_consequence: The next conflict becomes financial rather than informational.

seasons.arc: Season 8 — The Bank of Infinity | Financial and political consequences of opening the Atlas come due.

episodes.title: Interest on the Void
episodes.premise: An interstellar bank charges compound penalties on nonexistent routes; PIP traces the original obligations.
episodes.canon_consequence: Jax discovers his own debt was bundled into the scheme.

episodes.title: The Star That Was Collateral
episodes.premise: A creditor threatens to seize fictional infrastructure against an impossible stellar ownership claim.
episodes.canon_consequence: An independent court voids the claim.

episodes.title: The Dividend of Darkness
episodes.setting: Dark-matter halo of the Milky Way (model)
episodes.premise: A fund markets unverified resource extraction; Mira exposes the mismatch between observations and promises.
episodes.canon_consequence: The fund's collapse threatens legitimate pensions.

episodes.title: The Invisible Banker
episodes.premise: A chain of shell companies obscures Voss's assets; Cass negotiates testimony from a bookkeeper.
episodes.canon_consequence: A lawful restitution case begins.

episodes.title: The Family Business
episodes.premise: Voss's heirs debate protecting the family or returning stolen assets; one secretly helps Veda.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew offers conditional cooperation, not blanket immunity.

episodes.title: The Ship That Cost Nothing
episodes.premise: A free transport offer carries hidden debt clauses; Jax refuses a seemingly perfect deal.
episodes.canon_consequence: PIP uncovers a creditor-operated gate network.

episodes.title: The Insurance of the End
episodes.premise: A broker sells fake guarantees against a stellar event of uncertain timing.
episodes.canon_consequence: Mira helps the community design contingency plans instead.

episodes.title: The Moon of Last Resort
episodes.premise: A former refuge becomes a financial haven; an honest administrator must separate savings from stolen funds.
episodes.canon_consequence: The coalition obtains a lawful freeze on disputed accounts.

episodes.title: The Grand Exchange
episodes.premise: Trading houses stage a liquidity crisis to force a merger; Jax convenes smaller operators.
episodes.canon_consequence: Independent shippers establish an emergency pool.

episodes.title: A Currency Called Trust
episodes.premise: A new clearing system excludes people without historical records; Veda proposes alternate evidence.
episodes.canon_consequence: Former refugees become full participants.

episodes.title: The Man Who Insured Himself Twice
episodes.premise: Two incompatible claims expose a staged loss; Cass retrieves a real witness.
episodes.canon_consequence: The remaining stolen assets can be traced.

episodes.title: An Honest Bankruptcy
episodes.premise: A failing independent operator refuses Voss's rescue terms; the crew negotiates orderly restructuring.
episodes.canon_consequence: The coalition gains a transport network not owned by the houses.

episodes.title: The Last Family Dinner
episodes.premise: Voss offers Jax control of the family empire in return for ending the investigation.
episodes.canon_consequence: Jax refuses; the family splits publicly.

episodes.title: The Price of Freedom
episodes.premise: The compensation fund cannot satisfy every victim immediately; Veda establishes a fair queue.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew's allies commit to long-term accountability.

episodes.title: The Bank Without a King
episodes.premise: A distributed clearing union replaces the gate monopoly; Voss disappears through an unregistered relay.
episodes.canon_consequence: The route is linked to an ancient Atlas fragment beyond the known network.

seasons.arc: Season 9 — The Deep Archive | Origins of the Atlas and competing visions of cosmic history emerge.

episodes.title: The First Cartographer
episodes.premise: A recovered artifact contains an early navigation convention, not an omniscient map.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew identifies a sequence of historical records.

episodes.title: The Library of Dust
episodes.premise: A dust-obscured archive can be read only using multiple observations; Veda decodes its index.
episodes.canon_consequence: The archive describes several independent civilizations.

episodes.title: The Census of Dead Stars
episodes.setting: White dwarf population of the Milky Way
episodes.premise: A historian extrapolates too confidently from incomplete data; Mira corrects the method.
episodes.canon_consequence: The team narrows the origin search without claiming real alien evidence.

episodes.title: The City Before the City
episodes.premise: A legend of an ancient capital conflicts with the archive; Cass finds a political forgery.
episodes.canon_consequence: The original network was built by rival cultures cooperating.

episodes.title: The Seven Travelers
episodes.setting: Seven-star asterism of the Big Dipper (sky chart)
episodes.premise: A story of seven founders becomes a clue only when read as symbolic literature.
episodes.canon_consequence: Anant distinguishes spiritual symbolism from astronomical association.

episodes.title: The Star with No King
episodes.premise: A fictional itinerant settlement refuses membership in any empire.
episodes.canon_consequence: It possesses a charter variant that omits the Custodian's office.

episodes.title: The End of the World, Again
episodes.premise: A cosmic-cycle narrative is mistaken for a prediction; Veda separates myth and measured evidence.
episodes.canon_consequence: A recurring fictional maintenance cycle is identified.

episodes.title: The Giant's Notebook
episodes.premise: Micromegas returns with a notebook recording different scales of the ancient agreement.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew sees the charter was designed for radically different lives.

episodes.title: The Night Before the Sun
episodes.premise: A fictional cult claims ownership of a primordial signal; Mira explains what the observation actually measures.
episodes.canon_consequence: A coded modern addition, not the CMB itself, reveals a suspect.

episodes.title: A Message That Took Forever
episodes.premise: A genuine ancient-looking message may be replayed; PIP checks transmission and storage metadata.
episodes.canon_consequence: The original archive was mirrored rather than centrally stored.

episodes.title: The City of Unfinished Worlds
episodes.premise: A community of builders argues over who has the right to finish another's work.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew negotiates access to the final independent mirror.

episodes.title: The Prisoner of the Archive
episodes.premise: Voss is found hiding at a fictional relay; he claims the final key protects everyone.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew recovers his records without granting him control.

episodes.title: The Silence of the Founders
episodes.premise: No single founder speaks for the charter; the crew rejects a fabricated authoritative voice.
episodes.canon_consequence: Pell admits the Directorate knew the truth decades ago.

episodes.title: The Map That Refused a Master
episodes.premise: The mirror proves the Atlas was built to distribute trust, not reveal a literal edge of reality.
episodes.canon_consequence: The remaining key holders must ratify any changes.

episodes.title: The Last Blank Space
episodes.premise: Voss triggers a political emergency to reclaim control of the last network key.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew must convene a voluntary final settlement under time pressure.

seasons.arc: Season 10 — No One Owns the Universe | The charter is tested, the primary mystery resolves, a new series remains possible.

episodes.title: The Emergency Committee
episodes.premise: Pell calls a meeting after rival networks threaten to disconnect; the procedure itself excludes refugees.
episodes.canon_consequence: Veda demands direct representation.

episodes.title: The Return to Shackleton
episodes.premise: Jax revisits the original delivery site; the sender's identity is finally authenticated.
episodes.canon_consequence: The parcel was meant for a neutral audit, not a chosen hero.

episodes.title: The Sage's Question
episodes.premise: Anant asks whether the crew now seeks the very power it opposed.
episodes.canon_consequence: Jax relinquishes his unilateral claim to the key.

episodes.title: The Witnesses Arrive
episodes.premise: Witnesses from the first hearing return with independently preserved evidence.
episodes.canon_consequence: Pell's crimes and cooperation are judged separately.

episodes.title: The Seven Chairs
episodes.premise: Seven delegated communities disagree over the final charter; PIP exposes the misleading voting rule.
episodes.canon_consequence: A consent-based ratification mechanism is agreed.

episodes.title: The Clock Strikes Nothing
episodes.premise: A forged deadline attempts to rush the vote; Mira validates the timing chain.
episodes.canon_consequence: Communities receive time to make informed decisions.

episodes.title: The Most Expensive Apology
episodes.premise: The merchant houses propose symbolic apologies without restitution; Cass insists on enforceable commitments.
episodes.canon_consequence: A real compensation mechanism is funded.

episodes.title: The Man Without an Empire
episodes.premise: Voss tries to make a final bargain using the missing records of his own family.
episodes.canon_consequence: Jax preserves due process and refuses private immunity.

episodes.title: The Right to Disappear
episodes.premise: One refuge chooses not to participate in the public network; other delegates demand its location.
episodes.canon_consequence: The charter formally protects voluntary non-disclosure.

episodes.title: The Republic of Wrong Answers
episodes.premise: A policy error threatens confidence in the new council; Mira makes its correction public.
episodes.canon_consequence: The council adopts independent review rather than infallibility.

episodes.title: The Ledger Is Not the Law
episodes.premise: A legitimate claimant is rejected by an old record; Veda proves a database cannot replace justice.
episodes.canon_consequence: An appeal system is established.

episodes.title: The Last Vote
episodes.premise: The independent delegates ratify the amended charter despite Voss's final objections.
episodes.canon_consequence: No faction controls the Atlas alone.

episodes.title: A Universe of Its Own
episodes.premise: A message from an unconnected community offers a voluntary first exchange.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew accepts without demanding membership.

episodes.title: The Invoice at the End of the Universe
episodes.premise: PIP calculates years of unpaid crew expenses just as the others plan retirement.
episodes.canon_consequence: The crew chooses a new cooperative shipping company.

episodes.title: Return Address Unknown
episodes.setting: Deep sky: James Webb Deep Field imagery
episodes.premise: An unclaimed parcel arrives with an unfamiliar cipher; the crew debates whether to accept the job.
episodes.canon_consequence: The original mystery is resolved; a new adventure is optional, not a cliffhanger dependency.
